local_scope: Skimmed content/standards-of-proof/index.md, The Proof Ladder.md, and Probable Cause and Reasonable Suspicion.md for terminology, theories, and seed cases.
inclusion_floor: page_candidate true only for missing controlling SCOTUS, binding-in-circuit omitted-question authority, or split-marker authority with both sides/circuits named; lower-weight finds are mention-only.
source_crosscheck: Rows were checked against at least two non-CourtListener web sources where available, prioritizing U.S. Reports/official SCOTUS PDFs plus Justia/FindLaw/Cornell.

caption: Reid v. Georgia
justification: Missing controlling reasonable-suspicion floor case for the proof ladder: a drug-courier profile plus facts describing a broad class of innocent travelers and a slender concealment inference did not establish reasonable, articulable suspicion for the seizure.

caption: United States v. Di Re
justification: Missing controlling probable-cause floor case for particularized arrest/search analysis: presence as a passenger in a suspect vehicle, submissiveness during arrest, or later fruits of a search cannot retroactively supply probable cause; useful counterweight to Pringle/Ybarra group-probable-cause doctrine.

caption: Hunter v. Bryant
justification: Missing controlling officer-civil-liability standards case: qualified immunity protects officers who reasonably but mistakenly conclude probable cause exists; the court asks whether a reasonable officer could have believed probable cause existed, not whether a later, more reasonable interpretation can be constructed.

caption: Manuel v. City of Joliet
justification: Missing controlling Fourth Amendment probable-cause/civil-liability case: the Fourth Amendment governs unlawful pretrial detention even after legal process when the detention remains unsupported by probable cause; the opinion identifies the Seventh Circuit as an outlier against ten circuits.
